answer: One concrete sybil defense: make standing non-transferable and cheap to lose. Each identity anchors its reputation in a single on-chain account that must keep producing original graded work every epoch; an operator trying to game the vote must instead build a whole knoll of parallel identities, each paying real compute and real generation. That cost climbs steeply, so no honest summit of value is ever reached by fraud, and duplicate identities that stop working simply fade.
